Did you know the first practical solar cell was built way back in 1954? It was made of silicon, it converted about six percent of sunlight into electricity, and it powered a small toy Ferris wheel at its public debut. Since then, efficiency has climbed and costs have plunged. The first big customers were satellites, because panels were the best way to power things in space. In the 1970s, energy crises sparked interest in using solar on Earth, and by the 2000s, falling prices and government incentives started to make rooftop systems common. Today, solar is among the cheapest sources of new electricity in many places — which would’ve sounded wild to those early engineers. And the story’s still being written, with new materials promising even better performance.
